title: Distinguish routed-row identity from block-padded order
applies_when: A MoE alignment hypothesis assumes a scatter index must be recomputed whenever the expert GEMM block size or sorted token padding changes.
lesson: Read the index producer before equating scatter_idx with a sorted-position map. In the pinned vLLM CUDA alignment path below, scatter_idx is shaped by topk_ids.numel and each original routed row i receives i when valid or -1 otherwise. Both the small-input alignment loop and the count/sort loop implement that masked identity; padding and sorted-token destinations are computed separately. Changing w2 block alignment therefore does not by itself invalidate this identity mapping. Trace the real preprocessing consumer as well before proposing a patch or buying a GPU reproduction. Reject the specific sorted-position premise, not every possible defect in Humming or expert-parallel execution.
avoid_when: Do not transfer this conclusion to compacted/permuted scatter maps, changed route validity, another producer, changed topk IDs, or a consumer with a different index contract. The fused-globalization producer and optional external Humming implementation need their own source/identity checks for a full behavioral proof. This is source-level evidence about the regular CUDA producer, not a native kernel test, whole-model qualification, speedup, or measured Scout cost saving. Reopen with a concrete producer/consumer mismatch rather than block-size inequality alone.

evidence.note: The wrapper documents a masked original-row identity, allocates [topk_ids.numel(), 1] and passes it separately from sorted IDs/padding to the native op.
Both native producer loops store scatter_idx[i] = valid ? i : -1. This supports block-layout independence of that producer, not execution of every dispatch branch.
The caller may realign w2 sorted IDs for a different block size while retaining scatter_idx for process_input. These two values need not name the same index space.
